text:
A Surprise

        Today I received your letter. I have read it
with astonishment, for you say you
        are returning,
and I still have not recovered from the surprise...
It has been so long since
        I have lived without surprises!


"That at last you are coming to see me..., that so long
was the separation..." I advise you,
do not come, you would suffer a bitter
disillusion: you would
        find me old.


And like an old man, now, I have called myself
to quiet, and except
        —always the past!—
for one or another memory that on my forehead


puts some wrinkle of sadness,
I cannot complain:
        tranquilly
I smoke my pipe and drink my beer.

translation.title: That Time Your Memory Came
translation.editorial_note: The catalog title differs from the body, which begins 'A Surprise'; this translation preserves the body text.
